{"thought": "Looking at the code, each operator in a font dict causes `dictval.add_op(op, env.substr)` to be called, which pushes to the `values` vector. So if a font dict has more than 8 operators, `values` will grow beyond its static_array and allocate on the heap.

For the double-free to trigger:
1. CFF1 CID font with fdCount > 8 (to force fontDicts vector to reallocate from static to heap)
2. At least one of the first 8 font dicts needs > 8 operators (to get values.arrayZ_ allocated on heap)

But actually, a typical font dict only has a few operators (Private, FontName, FontMatrix, PaintType). To get > 8 operators in a single font dict, I'd need to repeat operators or use other dict operators.

Actually, looking at the `default` case in `CFF1FontDictOpSet::process_op`:
```cpp
default:
  DictOpSet::process_op (op, env);
  if (!env.argStack.is_empty ()) return;
  break;
```

When `!env.argStack.is_empty()`, it returns WITHOUT calling `dictval.add_op`. So for most operators in the default case, if the argStack still has items, the op isn't added. 

Let me look at DictOpSet::process_op to see what operators it handles.
